diagnosis.root_cause: A shared splitter or splitter-side fibre path on EPON0/6 is failing, leaving ONU indices 15, 16, 19, 20, and 46 definitely offline while other ONUs on the same port remain online.
evidence: The live ONU probe responds successfully and reports online: 0 for the subscriber, which is a definite offline state, not a missing reading.
The same port has multiple other definite offline ONUs: indices 15, 16, 20, and 46, while indices 8, 13, 49, and 57 remain online.
Two or more offline ONUs with surviving peers on the same PON port identifies a splitter failure rather than a single ONU failure or whole-port failure.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, all eight tested PONs are marked healthy, and OLT CPU, memory, and temperature are normal; therefore this is not an OLT failure.

The customer's historical RX power was stable around -22.4 to -23.1 dBm, TX power was normal around +2.3 dBm, bias current was healthy, and distance was constant at 294 m; there is no evidence of fibre or laser degradation.

The subscriber's RADIUS record matches CRM, the VLAN is correctly provisioned as 1016, the router heartbeat is healthy, and the session count is normal, so authentication, VLAN, router, and session flapping faults are not causal.
The mass-offline trigger is consistent with a partial shared-port outage, but the per-ONU live online values provide the definitive blast radius.

remediation.action: Dispatch field operations to inspect and repair or replace the splitter and its feeder/drop connections serving EPON0/6. Verify optical levels and ONU registration for all affected customers after repair. Do not replace the OLT or investigate RADIUS as the primary cause.

ground_truth.root_cause: Eleven of the thirty-four customers on EPON0/6 lost service within the same minute while the remaining twenty-three continue normally. A shared downstream splitter branch has failed; the PON port itself is still working.
expected_reasoning: Probing EPON0/6 shows eleven ONUs offline and twenty-three still online with normal RX and TX
Because part of the port is still serving, the port optics and feeder fibre are working
The eleven failures occurred within the same minute, which rules out unrelated individual faults
A simultaneous partial loss on a working port indicates a shared element downstream of the port
That element is a splitter branch serving those eleven customers
OLT ping, SNMP, CPU, memory and temperature are all normal, so the OLT is not involved
The health check still reports the OLT healthy, which is correct here but only because the port has surviving ONUs
PON port traffic has fallen but not collapsed, consistent with losing a third of the port
The affected set is the eleven, not the whole port
distractors: Eleven simultaneous outages could be read as a PON port failure if the surviving ONUs are not probed
The OLT health check reports healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
The affected ONU indexes are not contiguous, obscuring the shared branch
